blocks.text: We can use E° values to calculate the voltage of an electrochemical cell made up of two half-cells, even when neither of them is a standard hydrogen electrode. The voltage measured is the difference between the E° values of the two half-cells. We call this value the standard cell potential (E°Cell).

The voltage of this cell is +0.80 – (–0.76) = +1.56 V as in Figure 10.8 (b).

blocks.prompt: i) What is the function of salt bridge in the voltaic cell?
blocks.explanation: The salt bridge completes the circuit by letting ions move between the two half-cells, and it keeps both solutions electrically neutral (ionic balance), so the flow of electrons continues. Without a salt bridge charge builds up, the current stops and the voltage falls to zero.

blocks.prompt:
ii) Calculate the voltage of a cell having iron and copper electrodes.
Fe(s) ⇌ Fe²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ E° = – 0.44 V
Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ ⇌ Cu(s) E° = – 0.44 V
blocks.explanation:
E° of Fe²⁺/Fe = −0.44 V and E° of Cu²⁺/Cu = +0.34 V. Iron is more negative, so it is the anode:
E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = (+0.34) − (−0.44) = +0.78 V

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book gives E° = – 0.44 V for Cu²⁺/Cu here, repeating the value for iron. The E° of Cu²⁺/Cu is +0.34 V (Figure 10.9), so the iron-copper cell gives +0.34 – (–0.44) = +0.78 V.
The E° value for the Ag⁺/Ag half-cell is more positive than for the Zn²⁺/Zn half-cell. So, the Ag⁺/Ag half-cell is the positive pole and the Zn²⁺/Zn half-cell is the negative pole of the cell.
